narrative.overview: VerifyRuns looks like the receipt a careful engineer would print: near-black paper, one typeface for the claim, one for the evidence, and a single row of thirty squares that says everything before a word is read. The system is dark, flat and Swiss in temperament — solid surfaces, one-pixel hairlines, generous whitespace, no gradients, no glass, no decoration that is not data. Colour is rationed to two meanings: emerald means landed, red means did not. Everything else is a grey.
keyCharacteristics: Two-tone status vocabulary (emerald / red) on an otherwise achromatic zinc scale.
Three faces with fixed jobs: Outfit for claims, Manrope for prose and UI, JetBrains Mono for evidence.
Flat surfaces separated by hairlines; depth comes from tonal steps, never from shadow at rest.
The 30-square timeline is the signature component and appears identically on every surface that shows runs.
Motion is small and functional: a 160 ms colour transition, a 500 ms fade-up on entrance, a lift-and-glow on timeline hover.

rules.name: The Quiet-But-Legible Rule
rules.body: Every grey a user is expected to read clears 4.5:1 on the surface it sits on; quietness comes from size and weight, never from a darker grey.

rules.name: The Two-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Emerald and red mean PASS and FAIL and nothing else. Do not use emerald for primary action or red for delete — the primary button is white, and danger is a red-edged ghost so the filled reds stay reserved for verdicts.

rules.name: The Wash-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Status colour appears as a 10% wash with a 20–25% edge, except on the timeline square, where it is the only solid fill in the system.

rules.name: The Evidence-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the system observed — a timestamp, a count, a URL, a field name, a fingerprint — is set in JetBrains Mono. Anything the system says is set in Manrope.

rules.name: The Grey Second Clause Rule
rules.body: Headlines split into a claim and a consequence; the consequence is set in text-zinc-500 on its own line.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow until the user touches it or a modal opens. Depth is a tonal step and a hairline.

rules.name: The One Blur Rule
rules.body: backdrop-blur is permitted on the sticky nav and on modal scrims only; nowhere else is content allowed to show through a surface.

dos: Do set every observed value in JetBrains Mono, and every sentence the product speaks in Manrope.
Do keep the newest run on the right, padded with empties, on every timeline.
Do give PASS / FAIL a second channel beyond hue wherever verdict colour appears.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px hairline and a tonal step.
Do use the grey second clause for two-part headlines and a coloured eyebrow above them.
Do wrap verdict sentences in full; they are never truncated.
Do keep transitions specific at 140–160ms and entrance fades at 500ms.
Do keep data-testid on every interactive and key informational element.
Do teach the 3-step setup in empty states.
Do keep every colour behind a semantic token: dark-only is the current look, not a commitment.
Do render empty timeline slots as ghost squares (#1C1C1F) and caption the strip 'N of 30 runs' while N < 30.
donts: Don't use gradients on dark surfaces, glassmorphism, or translucent panels with content scrolling beneath.
Don't fill a button with emerald or red.
Don't seed empty states or examples with fake customers, logos or numbers.
Don't apply transition: all, bounce / elastic easing, or centre the whole app container.
Don't follow design_guidelines.json's rounded-none md:rounded-lg — the shipped system is 8 / 12px and that file is retired.
